parole.significato: a gift or message from heaven, a divine message, an oracle
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sanskrit आकाशवाणी (ākāśavāṇī, “celestial announcement from the sky, or voice from the sky/heaven; oracle”); probably through Hindi आकाशवाणी (ākāśvāṇī) or another Indic language with schwa deletion.

parole.significato: A blunt mace, originally from India and also common in Southeast Asia.
parole.testo: From Sanskrit गदा (gadā) or Hindi गदा (gadā).

parole.significato: A pillared hall or porch fronting a Hindu temple. It may be attached or detached from the building.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sanskrit मण्डप (maṇḍapa), मण्टप (maṇṭapa, “pavilion, mandapa”), a non-native word likely from the same source as मठ (maṭha, “hut, hermit's cottage”). Probably also borrowed from Hindi मंडप (maṇḍap) or another New Indo-Aryan language.
